title: How we know there is water
purpose: Teach the LCROSS impact result and the Chandrayaan-1 M3 ice map, and that evidence shows patchy ice, not a promise.

beats.label: measured
beats.credit: NASA LCROSS (Colaprete et al. 2010) · Cabeus crater

beats.label: measured

beats.map: Cold traps near the south pole

beats.label: measured
beats.sub: Ice is patchy, and lunar ice is not drinking water

captions: On {day}, NASA crashed a spent rocket stage into a dark crater.
A second spacecraft flew through the plume and measured it.
About {pct}% of it was water ice, give or take {unc}%.
Another instrument looked for ice right at the surface.
It found exposed ice in only {m3}% of the cold traps.
Some places hold plenty, most hold little, and none of it is ready to drink.
ends_on: Test before you trust: one sample does not tell you the whole crater.
